text:
rachel: quick summary from the kitelet-embed-int6 onboarding on the multi-holdout bench. dropping the highlights and a small repro snippet. @tom @emma please glance when you have a sec

tom: thanks rachel. top-line deltas?

rachel: float32 recall@10 = 0.688, int8-perchannel = 0.673, int6-dynamic = 0.679, int6-perchannel (calib 5k) = 0.682. latency: float32 15.6ms/embed, int8 8.7ms, int6 6.9ms. silhouette float32 0.30 -> int6-pc 0.28 -> int8-pc 0.25.

emma: int6-perchannel looks like a decent sweet spot. any per-lang oddities?

rachel: per-lang recall@10 deltas (int6-pc vs float32): en -0.006, fr -0.007, de -0.009, ja -0.027, zh -0.022. short-query (<8 tokens) recall@10 delta -0.018. long queries (>150 tokens) stable.

jules: ja/zh again. tokenization length skew? embedding norm tails?

rachel: yep token len median ja=6 zh=7 vs en=18. norm histogram attached in artifacts shows heavier tails for ja/zh; int quant clips the tails. increasing calib to 20k recovered ~0.009 recall@10 for ja.

tom: did you try hybrid fp16 matmul + int6 KV cache? saw that help elsewhere.

rachel: ran a quick hybrid run: hybrid-fp16-int6 recall@10 = 0.686, ja delta -0.014. latency hit ~+0.6ms vs pure int6 but still ~35% faster than float32.

emma: interesting. what about index config / PQ? sometimes OPQ+PQ can mask dimension noise.

rachel: main runs used HNSW M=16 ef_search=192, cosine, PQ off. OPQ+PQ(8) on top of int6-pc gave recall@10 0.678 and index size -3.5x. tradeoff sheet in artifacts.

jules: can you paste eval command so we can reproduce?

rachel: pasted below:

```
# kitelet quick eval
python eval_embeddings.py \\
  --model kitelet-embed-int6 \\
  --quant MODE \\
  --calib SAMPLES \\
  --holdout multi_holdouts.jsonl \\
  --index hnsw --M 16 --ef_search 192 --dist cosine \\
  --split short:lt8,long:gt150,langs:en,fr,de,ja,zh \\
  --seeds 4
```

rachel: MODE = float32 | int6-perchannel | int6-dynamic | int8-perchannel. SAMPLES = 5k/20k for sweeps.

ci-bot: nightly job kitelet-2026-04-22 completed  artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/kitelet/6201234567/ (metrics.csv, norms_hist.png, tsne_short_vs_long.png)

tom: plan / recommendation?

rachel: draft recommendation: Hosted default float16 (lowest variance + small latency win). Dedicated: enable int6-perchannel as opt-in with required calib >= 10k and per-lang monitoring; offer hybrid-fp16-int6 canary for customers with sensitive languages. Block naive int8-perchannel as default until ja/zh short-query gaps <1.5% abs.

emma: please add a small multilingual short-query golden set to the regression suite and record per-seed stds in the PR.

rachel: will do. PR with full metrics, seed variance, and reproducible scripts coming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/1101

jules: thanks, will review the PR when CI finishes.

rachel: follow-ups: (1) calib sweep 1k/5k/10k/20k, (2) hybrid latency microbench, (3) OPQ+PQ ablation. posting results back here. :white_check_mark:
